summary: PGNY's FY2023 10-K (filed Feb 29, 2024) and Q1 2024 10-Q (filed May 10, 2024 — five days before the cutoff) describe a profitable, debt-free, Big-4-audited fertility-benefits manager with a clean ICFR opinion, declining customer concentration, growing membership, and $370M of liquidity. The -37.6% drawdown is NOT a solvency or accounting-quality event — it is a growth-deceleration repricing: revenue growth collapsed from +38.3% (FY2023) to +7.6% (Q1 2024) on +19% member growth, implying ~-13% YoY revenue-per-member compression that the MD&A does not surface. The forensic-disclosure findings are Mode-B governance signals tucked into the May 10 10-Q: (1) the Compensation Committee adopted a first-time Executive Severance Plan for EVP+ on May 9, 2024 — six days before the cutoff — providing 12 months of base salary plus accelerated vesting, with no contemporaneous restructuring announced; (2) the CEO adopted a new 10b5-1 trading plan in Q1 2024 to sell up to 1,195,000 shares (~$45M) over a 13-month window ending April 30, 2025; (3) management did NOT update the reproductive-rights risk factor to address the Feb 2024 Alabama Supreme Court IVF ruling despite filing both reports after it. These signals are not lying — they are coherent senior-team preparation that the issuer narrative does not contextualize. The bullish counter-signals are real: aggressive buyback execution at $36.27 (net share-count reduction first time since IPO), no debt, declining concentration, and a clean Big-4 ICFR opinion. Verdict: NEUTRAL — the framework's exclusion-of-liars discipline does NOT catch PGNY (audit clean, balance sheet clean, no covenant or going-concern issues), but the Mode-B governance pattern argues against a long-tier rating until either Q2'24 reaccelerates or the CEO plan goes unused.
